title: BibCrit: An AI-Assisted Web Application for Biblical Textual Criticism
description:
This is the canonical record description. It is maintained in .zenodo.json in the repository and is applied automatically to every release — edit the “What's new” line below as part of each release commit.

What's new in this release: Added the LXX Manuscript Witnesses tool (the fifteenth tool), which analyzes significant divergences among the great Septuagint uncial codices — Vaticanus (B), Sinaiticus (א), and Alexandrinus (A) — for any passage.

BibCrit is an open-source, browser-based toolkit that applies large language model analysis to the methods and problems of biblical textual criticism. It requires no software installation and streams structured scholarly analysis in real time via Server-Sent Events. The application operates fully in English and Spanish, with AI-generated analysis cached and translated server-side.

The application integrates fifteen tools in a single interface:

  1. MT/LXX Divergence Analyzer — word-level comparison classifying divergences as translation technique, theological tendency, scribal error, or evidence for a divergent Hebrew Vorlage
  2. Back-Translation Workbench — word-by-word retroversion following Tov's methodology with confidence levels
  3. Scribal Tendency Profiler — five-axis radar chart scoring translator performance on literalness and other metrics
  4. Numerical Discrepancy Modeler — analysis of numerical divergences across witnesses
  5. Ancient Witness Bridge (DSS) — comparison across Dead Sea Scrolls, Samaritan Pentateuch, Peshitta, MT, and LXX
  6. Theological Revision Detector — identification of theologically motivated alterations
  7. Patristic Citation Tracker — analysis of Church Father citations through the 5th century
  8. Manuscript Genealogy — stemmatic visualization of textual transmission
  9. NT Use of OT Analyzer — identification of OT allusions in NT passages and their text-form (MT, LXX, or independent)
  10. Chiasm & Literary Structure Detector — detection of chiastic and concentric patterns
  11. Source Criticism Tool — attribution to documentary sources (J/E/D/P) via linguistic analysis
  12. Targum Comparator — analysis of Targum Onkelos and Jonathan renderings against MT and LXX
  13. NT Textual Tradition Analyzer — manuscript family attestation with Metzger A/B/C/D ratings
  14. Second Temple Literature Bridge — mapping allusions to 1 Enoch, Jubilees, Sirach, 4 Ezra, and Tobit
  15. LXX Manuscript Witnesses — analysis of divergences among the Vaticanus, Sinaiticus, and Alexandrinus uncials, with per-finding confidence and lacuna flags

Architecture. Python/Flask backend; the Anthropic Claude API (model claude-opus-4-7) generates all analytical content. Results are cached in Supabase with a disk JSON fallback, keyed by SHA-256 of reference, tool, prompt version, and model. Prompt templates are versioned and scholarly-grounded (Tov, Metzger, the Göttingen LXX apparatus, and others). A monthly budget cap prevents runaway API spend during public access.

Scholarly integrity. All AI-generated analysis is clearly attributed as such in the interface, and users are advised to verify results against primary sources and critical editions. The AI is not used for corpus ingestion, cache management, or any deterministic processing.

Languages. English and Spanish (append ?lang=es to any URL).

License. Apache 2.0 (code). See LICENSE-DATA.md in the repository for per-corpus data licensing.
